label: input token w in the original phase
explanation: A token detector for w. It fires on every original-phase step whose input is w (dev precision 1.0, recall 0.998) and never on any other input token. It does NOT fire on w fed back as input during the copy phase, except for 232 tiny activations (<0.06 of max) on an echoed w at recall_idx 1 in very short sequences that began with w. Magnitude is largest (about max) when w is the first token (t=0). In the sampled examples it is lower when w comes later in the sequence (about 0.9 at t=2, 0.4-0.6 near the end) and lower for a second occurrence of w (in_first=0 carries 7% of the mass versus 10% of the activations).

issues: No systematic counterexample found. On test: precision 1.000, recall 0.998, F1 0.999, mass recall 0.99995, 0 false positives. Every missed activation is at the copy step (L=3, step 4, recall_idx 1) where the echoed input is w and the sequence started with w, and together they carry about 0% of the mass.
Copy-phase w does not fire: (phase==2)&(in_tok==w) has precision 0.002 and mass recall 5e-5. The profile shows in_tok==w active at only 0.543 overall, so most copy-phase w inputs are silent.

Magnitude claims hold. Mass share falls with t (0.202 at t=0 down to 0.007 at t=8) while the rate per original position stays flat at 0.033-0.034. in_first=0 makes up about 10% of activations but 7.2% of the mass. Low-quartile examples are late-position w (0.4-0.6).
Minor: the label 'input token w in the original phase' is accurate. One could add that magnitude decays with position, but the explanation already covers it.
